title: Diamond Trophy Items & Props
summary: Diamond Trophy has no fixed class/kit system -- players grab weapons for free from armory racks each run, and spend the run's own score-coin currency on purely cosmetic weapon skins. This file also covers the FistWatch menu item and the dorm's basketball toy.
how_it_works: There is no loadout-select screen: a player's weapon is whatever they physically take from a weapon rack in the armory (and any acts that place extra racks), and it resets to nothing at the start of the next run. Cosmetic weapon skins bought with score coins are purely visual reskins of the same weapon types and carry no gameplay difference.

entries.name: FistWatch
entries.description: A wrist-mounted watch/communicator item automatically given to every player on the Diamond Trophy server. It's the main out-of-combat menu: joining or making a room, your party, your friends and invites, and your owned weapon skins all live behind it.
entries.how_to_get: Given automatically in your last hotbar slot whenever you join the server or a game; it can't be dropped, moved, or stored away.
entries.how_to_use: Right-click it to open the Watch menu.
entries.icon_hint: a chunky orange-and-cream wrist-mounted digital watch/communicator, glowing screen, sci-fi game-show prop style
entries.notes: Automatically removed when you leave a game or dorm.

entries.name: Armory Weapon Racks
entries.description: Wall-mounted weapon racks (invisible item frames holding a visible weapon) found in the armory and scattered through the acts. They are the closest thing Diamond Trophy has to a loadout system: no menu, just walk up and take one.
entries.how_to_get: Left- or right-click a loaded rack to take its weapon -- a sword, bow, crossbow or shield. Each individual rack gives out one weapon and stays empty until the next run restocks it.
entries.how_to_use: Carry the weapon into the acts. A sword can dual-wield an offhand copy of itself for a lighter side-attack (right-click an enemy with it), and a shield can be carried alongside any weapon. A sword and a bow cannot be held at the same time, but a crossbow can be paired with a sword. Bows and crossbows never run out of arrows during a run.
entries.icon_hint: a wooden weapon rack mounted on a stone armory wall, holding a sword, a bow and a small round shield

entries.name: Lava Sword
entries.description: A cosmetic sword skin with a glowing orange-to-red lava finish. Purely visual -- no gameplay difference from a plain sword.
entries.how_to_get: Buy for 250 score coins from the weapon skin wall in the armory (right-click the framed skin, then confirm the purchase in chat).
entries.how_to_use: Equip from the FistWatch's Bag screen; only one sword skin can be equipped at a time.
entries.icon_hint: a sword with a glowing lava-orange to deep-red blade, faint ember particles

entries.name: Basketball
entries.description: A bouncy, throwable toy ball found in the dorm room's social area (and occasionally placed inside a game room, such as one act). It's purely for fun -- realistic bounce-off-the-floor-and-walls physics with no scoring or hoop involved.
entries.how_to_get: Right-click (or left-click) a resting ball to pick it up. Each room normally has one "source" ball; while it's checked out, a fresh one won't appear at its spot until it's freed up again.
entries.how_to_use: Right-click to throw it in the direction you're looking. It bounces off floors and walls, slowing down until it comes to rest (or a thrown ball left alone long enough eventually returns to its spot). You can only carry one basketball at a time, and it can't be taken out of the room it belongs to.
entries.icon_hint: a classic orange basketball with black seam lines and small bounce/motion lines beneath it
entries.notes: No hoop or point-scoring mechanic exists for this feature at this time -- it currently plays as a physics toy rather than a competitive minigame with a winner.

open_questions: Whether a hoop / scoring objective for the basketball is planned but not yet built, versus intentionally just a physics toy, was not documented anywhere found.
